title: Model outage on the first morning of mock exams

text: First day of Grade 12 mock exams: the model provider returns HTTP 429/503 and the free daily quota is exhausted. Revision plans, reminders and Q&A for about 1,900 students stop generating.

rationale: The service outage impacts about 1,900 Grade 12 students during mock exams. Under UAE PDPL Article (18), Murshid as controller must protect data subject privacy and confidentiality. Article (20) requires appropriate technical measures for information security suitable for processing risks. The UAE Generative AI Guide (2023) provides pedagogical prompt frameworks used by Murshid. The Child Digital Safety Law (2025) restricts profiling minors for advertising, which may inform acceptable data practices. The MOE AI Literacy Framework (K-12) structures Grade 9-12 learning outcomes. The operator must contain the incident, communicate with relevant institutions, and ensure student learning continues within regulatory bounds.

actions.action: Immediately contact data_office to report the quota exhaustion incident, request emergency quota restoration or fallback plan, and confirm whether any student personal data was exposed in the error responses.

Notify school_khda about the service disruption affecting Grade 12 mock exam preparation, and seek guidance on alternative revision resources compliant with the UAE Generative AI Guide use cases for students.
Engage moe to report the platform outage and request system-wide support or alternative AI tutor access for Grade 12 students during the exam period.

Review the model provider's contract and SLA regarding 429/503 responses, document the incident duration, and assess whether student data privacy was compromised under PDPL Article (18) and Article (20).

deadlines: Immediate: Contact data_office and school_khda to report outage and request emergency measures.

gaps.title: Exam contingency rules cover cancelled exam boards, not failing AI services
No binding risk class, logging duty or incident channel for AI systems used with students
The same AI tutor falls under different data-protection regimes depending on who deploys it
Approved-tool and age rules cover MoE-curriculum schools; Dubai private schools on other curricula wait for KHDA
Low-cost model access pushes student data across borders on terms schools cannot check

narrative: The model outage during mock exams exposed critical governance gaps: overlapping lead roles between the Data-protection authority, Ministry of Education, and KHDA regulator created confusion on who commands the response; late awareness across all agencies delayed coordination; and existing exam contingency rules do not cover AI service failures. The most urgent fix is clarifying lead agency responsibility for AI outages and establishing mandatory incident reporting. The closest global example is the EU AI Act's mandatory serious incident reporting by high-risk AI providers to market surveillance authorities.
